newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate drops to 10.6 percent.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate drops to 10.6 percent.

text.p: The Croatian money market rate fell to 10.6 percent on Friday from 11.7 percent as some lenders trimmed their rates.
Daily settlements rose to 36.1 million kuna from Thursday's 26.8 million of which new placements accounted for 30.2 million.
Dealers said demand at 37.5 million kuna was not met in full despite good supply as banks wanted to secure funds for the weekend.
Weighted call money rate fell 30 basis points to 10.7 percent. Rates for term loans varied between 9.0 percent for insurers' money and 16 percent for one 30-day fresh placement.

The central bank calculated its kuna midrates for the weekend and Monday weaker at 6.0845 versus 6.0525 against the dollar and at 3.5707 versus 3.5744 against the German mark. -- Laura Lui, Zagreb newsroom, 385-1-4557075
